mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be negative due to tightened financing conditions affecting corporate investment and consumer spending.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior month's return (t-test p > 0.05), or the FEDFUNDS change is not above 0.25% in any month during the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.3% for two consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as expectations of future disinflation boost equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < prev(CPIAUCSL) and CPIAUCSL < prev(prev(CPIAUCSL)) by ≥ 0.3%
failure_condition: In regimes where CPIAUCSL does not decline by ≥ 0.3% for two consecutive months, or the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p < 0.05) relative to the month before the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in employment growth (PAYEMS) of at least 10% month-over-month is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as labor market strength supports corporate optimism.
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive months with PAYEMS growth ≥ 10% MoM, the 5-day forward return is never statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) unexpectedly exceeds its prior month by at least 2% and coincides with rising retail sales (HOUST), the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is more likely to be positive, reflecting stronger aggregate demand.
regime_hint: Surge in supply and demand momentum
failure_condition: In 100 matched INDPRO/HOUST positive surprise pairs, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of 3% or more over three consecutive months predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as it signals weakening manufacturing capacity and demand absorption.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < prev(INDPRO) * 0.97 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During such a 3-month INDPRO decline regime, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in 80% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment claims (UNRATE) below 4% and a decline in labor force participation (PAYEMS < prev(PAYEMS) by 2%) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to recessionary labor market signals.
failure_condition: Over 50 such UNRATE/PAYEMS cross-patterns, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail activity (HOUST) exceeds expectations by at least 5% and coincides with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE < prev(UNRATE) - 0.2%), the S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days tends to be positive, reflecting strong consumer confidence and labor market resilience.
failure_condition: In 100 such HOUST/UNRATE positive surprise pairs, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (Rank IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of falling inflation (CPIAUCSL declining by ≥ 0.2% month-over-month for 4 consecutive months) without a corresponding rise in interest rates (FEDFUNDS), the S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days tends to be positive as markets anticipate disinflation and rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < prev(CPIAUCSL) * 0.98 for 4 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS <= prev(FEDFUNDS)
failure_condition: In 50 such CPIAUCSL/FEDFUNDS regimes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).
